EDIT: Am I doing asatru wrong, and am I too sensitive?

Short answer: there are a lot of jerks on the internet, that includes Asatru groups... Our vision within /v/asatru is to give everyone a place to learn and ask stupid questions, because we feel there is no one right answer to most questions. It's a place for discussion. A lot of groups on the internet have a certain background (i.e. reconstructionalism) and some of those backgrounds carry certain dogma's (you can only do x ritual on y day, by speaking old norse verses of z etc etc) and they have no respect for people who have different views. We welcome everyones views, but we do not tolerate blatant racism.

For the long answer...

There are a lot of different groups within heathenry, or "germanic neopaganism" (the umbrella term). I've been around tons of online groups and real-life kindreds... When joining a facebook group or something, it is of utmost importance that you take a critical look at what kind of group you are dealing with, since you might not want to associate yourself with certain groups, or maybe have different beliefs or a different focus all together. Keep in mind that most of these groups go along with eachother just fine, it's mainly the universalists versus the genetics and the recons versus the revivalists or modernists.

Some of these groups have geographical differences, in example:

Asatru - Icelandic Heathenry, but also often used as synonym for general Germanic Neopaganism by American kindreds

Forn Sed - Scandanavian (mainly Danish and Swedish)

Anglo-Saxon - “English” heathenism, focussed on Anglo-Saxon belief system

And then there are also a couple of tribe-specific religions, such as:

Frankish Heathenry - Focussed on culture of the Franks (Germany, Netherlands, Belgium and France)

Saxon Heathenry - Fosussed on the culture of the Saxon tribes (Netherlands, Germany)

And then there are those with different views or practice:

Theodism - used by followers of Anglo-Saxon heathenry, often also used by Folkish or Tribal heathens who focus on one specific tribe (Norman, Angle, Continental Saxon, Alemannic etc)

Folktro - Most Scandanavian kindreds are Folktro. Heathenry is a living tradition and doesn’t need to be based on academic research or the Edda’s, sometimes used as word for folkish scandanavian heathenry.

Reconstructionalism - reconstructing the worldview and practices of the pre-christian religion of Germanic tribes by intensive study, often limited to only one geographical location and language

Revivalism - reviving the old pre-christian religion of Germanic tribes of the Iron Age as a contemporary religion

Modernist - seeing Heathenry as a modern contemporary religion with the constraints of modern day

Universalism - cultural and moral relativism, anyone can practice heathenry

and those who throw race or genetics into the mix:

Geneticist - the receptivity of heathen spiritualism is passed on trough genetic inheritance

Folkish - believe heathenry is an ethnic religion because it revolves around worshipping the ancestors and thus should only be practiced by people with Germanic and/or Scandanavian blood

Tribalism - to practice heathenry you must have Germanic or Sandanavian blood OR you must be adopted into the culture (in example by swearing an oath of loyalty to a tribalist kindred)

Odinism - Emphasis om Odin and Frigg, not focussed on academic research or the edda’s, most Odinists thinks only caucasians can be heathen

Wotanism - Odinism with more emphasis on white nationalism and white seperatism

Unfortunatly as you can see, some of these groups that call themselves heathen, have a racist ideology. So you can imagine that most people don't really get along with Odinists, which is basically the new KKK and a lot of white supremists and neo-nazi's are drawn to Odinism. But some peoples views differ greatly on how they practice, so most recons don't get along really well with revivalists, in example, but there are a lot of people who are teodish recons, so they do get along really well.

But wait, there's more!

There are also a lot of groups that aren't really a part of germanic neopaganism, but are somehow connected. So then again, all groups above sometimes make fun of the groups below here, because they're taking some elements of heathenry and making it their own (even though that is basically also what most groups above do...) To name a couple of examples you might come across:

Vanatru - a deviation of “Asatru” (true to the Aesir), but then “True to the Vanir”

Rokkatru - worship of Jotun Gods (giants)

Lokean - worship of Loki

Multi-tradition - worship of Norse Gods next to Gods of other religions

And this all is probably just the tip of the ice berg ;)

  2. Folding or telescoping (collapsible) stock, which reduces the overall length of the firearm
  3. Pistol grip, whether rifle, shotgun, or pistol
  4. Bayonet lug, which allows the mounting of a bayonet
  5. Threaded barrel, which can accept devices such as a flash suppressor, Suppressor, compensator or muzzle brake
  6. Grenade launcher
  7. Barrel shroud, which prevents burning of shooter's arm or hand as a safety device.

While all of the above characteristics are functional in nature, they have been selected as determining features based largely on appearance, because they make guns look scary.

"Assault rifles" can include both semi-automatic and full-automatic rifles. Technically, if the term "assault rifle" is to be taken literally, any rifle used to commit an act of violence or assault is an "assault rifle". Just as a chair used to beat a victim could be termed an "assault chair". The term "assault rifle" is almost meaningless aside from serving as a political tool.

  1. Any weapon which shoots, is designed to shoot, or can be readily restored to shoot, automatically more than one shot without manual reloading, by a single function of the trigger.

  2. The frame or receiver of any such weapon.

  3. Any part designed and intended solely and exclusively or combination of parts designed and intended for use in converting a weapon into a machinegun.

  4. Any combination of parts from which a machinegun can be assembled if such parts are in the possession or under the control of a person.
